summary: My v1 advisory is repaired past what I asked for. I asked that the two DR-124 classes be named as D-002 State names them; v2 instead splits them into two separate permitted surfaces, P-002-3 for rebuildable cache/index and a new P-002-4 for operational metadata, each carrying its own class lifecycle verbatim from file 04, and P-002-4 states the anti-collapse explicitly: 'Not rebuildable. Rebuildability stays on P-002-3's cache/index class only.' It further adds that DR-124 remains OPEN and that this disposition assigns no class, owner, writer or lifecycle for any byte, with a matching refusal. A path-level diff shows REMOVED 0, and I traced both whole-document token losses to the repair itself rather than to substance dropped: the per-surface exclusions that moved out of P-002-3's bound are covered at document level, and the concepts survive. Every other axis holds, file 04 is newly pinned at a digest matching live, and the disposition still forecloses my own ACCEPT being read as owner recording.

C2-RB002-A1 is repaired, and by a stronger method than my remedy. I asked for the DR-004 sibling's phrasing to be copied. Instead the two classes became two surfaces. P-002-3 is now 'Rebuildable cache/index working copy of an analysis result (DR-124 class D-002 includes)' whose bound reproduces file 04's class-3 rule -- 'May be discarded and regenerated. A cache hit equals recomputation. Provenance and corruption tests must prove no authority and no hidden input' against file 04's 'discarded/rebuilt; provenance and corruption tests prove no authority or hidden input'. P-002-4 is new: 'Operational metadata (DR-124 class D-002 includes) for the non-semantic invocation/audit envelope', whose bound reproduces class 4's rule -- 'excluded from Plan/Run unless an applied owner explicitly promotes a field' against file 04's 'Excluded from Plan/Run unless an applied owner expl…'.

The specific collapse I raised is now foreclosed in words rather than merely avoided: P-002-4 states 'Not rebuildable. Rebuildability stays on P-002-3's cache/index class only', and P-002-3 states 'This is not Operational metadata'. The two surfaces exclude each other in both directions.

The repair also adds a limit I did not ask for and would have wanted: 'DR-124 remains OPEN and must assign every persisted byte one class, owner, writer, and lifecycle before blueprint work; this disposition does not perform that assignment', with a matching refusal 'Does not assign DR-124 class/owner/writer/lifecycle for any byte.'

Both classes are the ones adopted D-002 State permits, which I re-read at the bytes: 'State: local, non-authoritative only — rebuildable cache/index and operational metadata classes (DR-124)'. Neither surface admits a class D-002 excludes, and D-002's own exclusion of the analysis-affecting durable state class is respected.

A path-flattening diff of v1 against v2 gives REMOVED 0, ADDED 21, CHANGED 5. I then ran a whole-document token-loss pass, which is where a rewritten bound can quietly shed an exclusion. Two tokens are lost, 'local' and 'replay-as-authority', and I traced both. 'Not replay-as-authority' and 'Not a sealed Run' left P-002-3's per-surface bound, and both are covered at document level by whatMustNotBePretendedSettled's 'Authoritative sealed closure, replay, or evidence custody (D-002 State: OUT of the preview)'; the new bound independently requires proof of 'no authority', which is the same constraint stated as a test. 'local' left P-002-3's surface title but survives at P-002-4's 'Host-local and non-authoritative', and the whole disposition is scoped to 'architecture preview (D-002 / D-018) only', where D-002 State supplies locality for both classes. I record this as examined and declined rather than as a finding.

verdictNote: ACCEPT with zero findings. My advisory asked for a naming fix and got a structural one: two classes became two surfaces, each bound by its own file-04 lifecycle, with reciprocal exclusions and an explicit statement that rebuildability belongs only to the cache/index class. I checked the thing a wholesale rewrite most often gets wrong -- whether an exclusion was shed while the prose improved -- and the two tokens the document lost are both covered elsewhere, one by a document-level refusal and one by the preview's own D-002 scope. I also verified the newly pinned file 04 against live bytes rather than accepting the pin, since the repair's authority now rests on it.
